goal: A 5-minute playable vertical slice that captures the core fantasy of Palworld: a beautiful third-person world, charming creatures, meaningful interaction, and believable creature behaviour.
bar: The real Palworld. A fresh critic is shown our capture beside an official Palworld frame — same shot type, same resolution, same format, labels stripped, order shuffled — and asked which one is the shipped commercial game. We are done when critics stop reliably picking correctly.
currentState: round 2 — rendering pipeline: fix overexposure, zero shadow structure, flat desaturated grade
openGaps: Rendering pipeline blows the frame out: up to 47% clipped highlights, darkest pixel ~90-96/255 (no shadow structure anywhere), flat desaturated grade (~500-700 unique colors vs Palworld's 850-1600), low edge detail in creature portrait and dusk mid-ground. Every one of our 5 comp shots was correctly identified as NOT the commercial game.
Reference gap: only 1 of 17 official stills is early-game peaceful exploration, so interaction_feed has no honest comp and is judged on the art-direction rubric instead.
Reference gap: the trailer never shows a creature noticing an approaching player, so behaviour_approach has no fair comp either and is graded against the 12 written aliveness criteria.

rounds.title: Rendering pipeline: kill the blown-out wash, restore shadow structure and colour
rounds.summary: Blind critic B (pixel-forensic, 5/5 correct) proved our frames are destroyed by the render chain: 47% clipped highlights, no shadows (darkest pixel 96/255), flat palette (500-700 colors vs 850-1600), low detail. Runtime diagnostics show the scene is rich (142 draws, 586k tris, 8860 grass blades) and post is enabled with ACES — so the image is being wrecked between scene render and final pixels. Suspects: colour-space double-encoding (SRGB output + HalfFloat RT + manual ACES/linearToSRGB re-applied), sun intensity 3.52 in physical-light units, and shadow maps not reaching materials. A deep builder owns the fix and must prove it with forensic deltas, not opinion.

rounds.title: Nine systems built in parallel, then integrated
rounds.summary: Nine builder agents with fresh context, each owning one disjoint system directory, each required to read the art-direction brief, look at the real reference screenshots, and verify against their own rendered output. Then an integration pass to make nine independent parts cohere. Integration capture succeeded (6 shots + 2 strips, all frames passed the probe), but blind A/B against real Palworld frames was 0/5: the rendering pipeline washes the image out.
improvements: All nine systems (world, sky, player, creatures, ai, interaction, ui, audio, post) built and integrated; capture reports OK with 143-170 draws and 590-830k triangles
Runtime diagnostics prove the scene is content-rich (8860 grass blades, 266 trees, 306 rocks, 14 creatures) and the post chain runs with zero failures
gaps: Blind A/B verdict 0/5: every studio frame correctly identified as not-the-commercial-game (overexposure, no shadows, flat grade, low detail)

rounds.title: Scaffold, capture harness, blind-A/B tooling
rounds.summary: Engine, system contracts and the deterministic capture harness are working. First run silently screenshotted the loading overlay and still reported OK — fixed, and a frame probe now fails any capture that is blank, uniform, or still showing an overlay.
improvements: Fixed-timestep engine with a system registry; systems never import each other, so builder agents can own disjoint directories without conflicts
Deterministic seeded RNG and noise — same seed always produces the same world, which is what makes round-over-round A/B meaningful
Headless capture harness driving the game through the same input path a human uses
Matched-shot protocol: 6 staged stills + 2 motion strips
Blind A/B pack builder that normalises resolution/format/quality so critics judge the picture, not a technical tell
17 official Palworld reference stills acquired and readable by agents
gaps: Stub art across the board — this round only proves the measuring instruments work
